title: HNSW parameters
summary: HNSW has three knobs: m (links per node), efConstruction (build-time effort) and efSearch (query-time effort). They trade recall against memory, build time and latency, and the defaults differ by product.
useIf: You run an HNSW index and need to tune recall, latency or memory with evidence instead of guessing.
avoidIf: You have no exact-search baseline. Without it you cannot tell whether a change improved recall.

explain.md: **HNSW** (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is a layered graph where each vector links to some neighbours [[tr20]]. A query enters at the top layer, hops greedily toward the query, drops a layer, and at the bottom layer keeps a candidate list of the best vectors found so far. The size of that list is `efSearch`. The graph quality is set when you build it, by `m` and `efConstruction`.

The costs land at different times. Raising `m` connects each node better, which helps on clustered or high-dimension data, but every vector pays for it in memory. Raising `efConstruction` costs build time once. Raising `efSearch` costs time on every query. That asymmetry is why you tune `efSearch` first: it is the cheap knob to turn when you see a recall or latency problem.

explain.md: AI Search takes `metric` of `cosine`, `dotProduct`, `euclidean` or `hamming` and offers `hnsw` or `exhaustiveKnn` as algorithm kinds [[tr10]]. The pgvector and Qdrant defaults come from their documentation [[tr12]] [[tr35]]. An `efSearch` of 40 is normal in pgvector and below the minimum of 100 in AI Search, so copying a number between engines is a mistake.

steps.md: Run exact search on a sample of real queries to get true neighbours.

steps.md: Keep defaults for the build, sweep the query knob, record recall at k and p95 latency.

steps.md: If recall plateaus below target, raise `m` and `efConstruction`, rebuild, repeat.

pitfalls.symptom: Recall will not improve however high `efSearch` goes
pitfalls.cause: The graph was built with low `m` or `efConstruction`, so some neighbours are unreachable
pitfalls.fix: Raise `m` and `efConstruction` and rebuild, then re-sweep `efSearch`

pitfalls.symptom: Query latency doubled after a recall fix
pitfalls.cause: `efSearch` was raised, so each query explores more candidates
pitfalls.fix: Find the lowest `efSearch` that meets the recall target on your sample

pitfalls.symptom: Filtered queries return fewer than k rows in pgvector
pitfalls.cause: With default `hnsw.ef_search` of 40, filters apply after the index scan and discard most candidates
pitfalls.fix: Raise `ef_search`, enable iterative scans (0.8.0 and later) or use another filter strategy

pitfalls.symptom: A pgvector index build takes far longer after raising `ef_construction`
pitfalls.fix: Raise it only if recall demands it and plan build windows

scenarios.title: Recall is fine, latency is not
scenarios.situation: An HNSW index meets a recall target of 0.95 against exact search. Measured recall at the current setting is 0.99 and p95 latency exceeds the budget.
unknowns: How far above the target is recall at lower settings?
Is the latency from the index or the network?
scenarios.question: What do you change?

options.name: Lower `efSearch` step by step while tracking recall against the 0.95 target
options.why: It spends the surplus recall on latency, needs no rebuild and the sample shows where to stop.
options.tradeoff: Recall falls toward the target and the margin shrinks.

options.name: Add replicas or a bigger tier
options.why: Lowers latency under load without touching recall.
options.tradeoff: Higher cost, and it does not help single-query latency.

options.name: Rebuild with a higher `m` and `efConstruction`
options.why: Improves recall that is already enough and adds memory, which has no headroom.
options.tradeoff: Right when recall is below target at the highest acceptable `efSearch`.

flips.if: Latency is dominated by the embedding call, not search
flips.then: Tune the query embedding path before touching HNSW.

scenarios.takeaway: Spend surplus recall on latency with the query-time knob first.

scenarios.title: Recall plateaus at 0.90
scenarios.situation: On a 12 million vector index recall stays near 0.90 even with `efSearch` at 1,000, the product maximum. The target is 0.95. Memory has some headroom.
unknowns: Are filters in use during the test?
scenarios.question: What is the next step?

options.name: Raise `m` and `efConstruction`, rebuild, then re-sweep `efSearch`
options.why: A recall plateau at the top of the query range signals a weak graph, and the build knobs fix that.
options.tradeoff: More memory, a longer build and a rebuild.

options.name: Add oversampling and rescoring if the field is quantized
options.why: Recovers precision lost to compression if that is the cause.
options.tradeoff: Does not help if the graph itself is the limit.

options.name: Keep raising `efSearch`
options.why: It is already at the maximum, so there is nothing left to raise.
options.tradeoff: Right when `efSearch` is still far below its cap.

flips.if: The index uses binary quantization without rescoring
flips.then: Enable rescoring first, since compression may cause the plateau.
Combine a moderate `m` with quantization and rescoring.

scenarios.takeaway: When the query knob is exhausted, the build knobs are the lever.

quiz.q: Match each HNSW parameter to its main effect.

pairs.r: Links per node, affects recall and memory
Build-time candidates, affects graph quality and build time
Query-time candidate list, affects recall and latency
The similarity measure, such as cosine

quiz.explain: The three ef and m knobs act at different times: `m` and `efConstruction` at build, `efSearch` at query. `metric` chooses the similarity function.

quiz.q: Recall plateaus at 0.90 even with `efSearch` at its maximum. Which change most likely helps?
options: Switch the metric from cosine to dotProduct
quiz.explain: A plateau at the top of the query range means the graph is the limit, which the build parameters control. Lowering efSearch reduces recall, changing the metric changes semantics, and replicas affect throughput.

quiz.q: Which statements about HNSW defaults are correct?
options: A given `efSearch` value means the same in every engine
quiz.explain: The defaults are 500 in AI Search, 40 in pgvector and an `m` of 16 in pgvector. Values are not comparable across engines.
